{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012ZN7qTN36kcFSdQDXwCJi2","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# CorrecTek — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: http://www.correctek.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→CorrecTek is a niche EHR vendor based in Paducah, Kentucky, founded in 2006 and specializing in electronic health records for **correctional healthcare, juvenile detention, and behavioral health** settings. The company's tagline is \"EHR Your Way,\" emphasizing customizability. They serve over 120 organizations across 30+ U.S. states and territories, with over 200 correctional institutions reportedly using their platform. CorrecTek claims a 99% customer satisfaction rate and over 20 years of experience in the correctional health IT space.\n     9→\n    10→CorrecTek is a small, privately held company (headquartered at 2929 Broadway, Paducah, KY 42001). Based on ZoomInfo data, competitors include AltaPoint Data Systems, FoxFire Systems Group, ChartLogic, and The Joxel Group — all relatively small vendors. The company's president is Dan Jarrett. CorrecTek sells directly and also works with healthcare vendors who provide correctional healthcare services (e.g., companies that contract to run medical operations within jails/prisons). They specifically note a \"Corizon vs CorrecTek\" comparison page, suggesting they compete directly with Corizon Health (a major correctional healthcare provider with its own EHR).\n    11→\n    12→The product is offered as either a one-time purchase or a lease option. Hosting options include cloud-hosted (managed by Kalleo Technologies, their preferred option), hybrid (on-premise but Kalleo-managed), or self-hosted (on-premise, self-managed).\n    13→\n    14→## Product: Spark\n    15→\n    16→CHPL ID: 10274\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→Spark is CorrecTek's single EHR platform — it is the entire product, not a component of something larger. It is ONC-certified (version 7.1, certified 2020-01-14) and purpose-built for complex care environments, primarily correctional facilities (jails and prisons), juvenile detention centers, behavioral health programs, and other specialized residential treatment settings. The certified module IS the product. Spark is also EPCS-certified for electronic prescribing of controlled substances.\n    21→\n    22→The CHPL certification is broad, covering 30+ criteria across clinical data (a)(1)-(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1), EHI export (b)(10), bulk data (b)(11), clinical quality measures (c)(1), FHIR API (g)(7)+(g)(10), direct messaging (h)(1), and security/privacy criteria. This certification profile indicates a full-featured EHR, not just a narrow module.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→**Intended users** (per CHPL): \"Medical office personnel, including RNs, Providers, Admins and Support staff.\" In practice, given the correctional setting, this includes:\n    27→- **Nurses and medical staff** performing intake screenings, sick call, medication administration, and chronic care management\n    28→- **Physicians/providers** documenting encounters, ordering labs/imaging, prescribing medications\n    29→- **Behavioral/mental health clinicians** documenting behavioral health encounters (the correctional page explicitly mentions behavioral health records in the unified chart)\n    30→- **Dental providers** (dental records are mentioned as part of the unified patient chart)\n    31→- **Billing/administrative staff** managing claims, eligibility checks, and payment reconciliation\n    32→- **Facility administrators** using reporting and analytics tools for compliance oversight\n    33→\n    34→Customer base is overwhelmingly in **correctional and juvenile detention settings**: county jails, state prisons, juvenile detention centers, and residential treatment programs. The system supports compliance with correctional healthcare accreditation bodies including NCCHC (National Commission on Correctional Health Care), ACA (American Correctional Association), and AJA (American Jail Association).\n    35→\n    36→### Modules & Functionality\n    37→\n    38→**Charting & Clinical Documentation** (vendor Spark product page, correctional solutions page):\n    39→- Structured clinical documentation with customizable forms, templates, and workflows\n    40→- Emphasis on quick data entry through structured inputs and direct selections rather than manual typing\n    41→- Configurable patient intake workflows\n    42→- Audit-ready documentation to support compliance\n    43→\n    44→**Unified Health Record** (correctional and juvenile pages):\n    45→- Integrates medical, dental, and behavioral health records into a single unified patient chart\n    46→- Centralizes all patient data in one location\n    47→\n    48→**Medication Management** (correctional page, interfaces page):\n    49→- Electronic Medication Administration Record (eMAR) for accurate medication tracking\n    50→- EPCS-certified e-prescribing (including controlled substances)\n    51→- E-prescribing via NewCrop (required for Meaningful Use users, per mandatory disclosures page)\n    52→- Bidirectional pharmacy interfaces supporting medication orders, renewals, refills, drug substitutions, and barcoding\n    53→- SureScripts integration for querying 12-month prescription history\n    54→\n    55→**Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE)** (per CHPL criteria (a)(1)-(a)(3)):\n    56→- Medication orders\n    57→- Laboratory orders (sent directly to lab vendors, results received back into Spark)\n    58→- Imaging/radiology orders (sent to radiology vendors, interpretations and optional low-res images returned)\n    59→\n    60→**Drug Interaction Checking** (mandatory disclosures page, CHPL criteria (a)(4)):\n    61→- Clinical decision support for drug interactions\n    62→\n    63→**Integrated Billing** (Spark product page):\n    64→- Full billing cycle management within Spark — no external billing system needed\n    65→- Eligibility checks (real-time coverage verification)\n    66→- Automatic code assignment (billing codes applied automatically during documentation)\n    67→- Claim submission (Medicare, Medicaid, private insurance)\n    68→- ERA (Electronic Remittance Advice) posting — automated payment and adjustment application\n    69→- Specific support for Medicaid 1115 waiver programs (common in correctional healthcare where states use waivers to bill Medicaid for inmate healthcare)\n    70→- Charges feed interface that automates billing through commissary vendors\n    71→\n    72→**Sick Call Management** (interfaces page):\n    73→- Inmate sick call requests captured through phones, kiosks, or tablets are sent to Spark\n    74→- Optional confirmation and status updates back to inmates\n    75→\n    76→**Reporting & Analytics** (Spark product page, solutions page):\n    77→- Built-in reporting engine with hundreds of prebuilt report templates\n    78→- Reports across clinical, compliance, cost, and operational domains\n    79→- Automated reports for detailed analysis\n    80→- Optional CBI (CorrecTek Business Intelligence) Dashboard add-on powered by Microsoft Power BI for visual dashboards, drill-down analysis, and trend monitoring\n    81→\n    82→**Scheduling & Workflow** (various pages):\n    83→- Scheduling through structured inputs\n    84→- Task optimization through automation of redundant tasks\n    85→\n    86→**Compliance & Risk Management** (correctional page):\n    87→- Configurable workflows aligned with NCCHC, ACA, AJA accreditation requirements\n    88→- Detailed documentation for compliance and liability reduction\n    89→- Role-based access controls\n    90→- Comprehensive audit trail tracking all user activity\n    91→\n    92→**Juvenile-Specific Features** (juvenile solutions page):\n    93→- Release planning (coordination with case managers for resident release)\n    94→- Medication compliance tracking\n    95→- Patient portal for guardian access to resident records and consent\n    96→- Immunization registry verification and updates for state compliance\n    97→- Automated age-based preventative care (wellness checks)\n    98→- Resident tracking interfaces\n    99→\n   100→**Interoperability & Data Exchange** (interfaces page):\n   101→- C-CDA and PDF export (per mandatory disclosures)\n   102→- FHIR API access via \"Interoperability Engine\" (likely EMR Direct, per mandatory disclosures)\n   103→- Carequality network participation for nationwide health record sharing\n   104→- Health Information Exchange (HIE) — sending/receiving patient records with regional and state exchanges\n   105→- Direct messaging (h)(1) certification\n   106→- US Marshals documentation support for federal detainees\n   107→- Hospital interface for receiving lab results, transcriptions, and medical service records\n   108→- Immunization and cancer registry reporting to state systems\n   109→- AI/analytical tools interface (Spark does not include built-in clinical analysis; it interfaces with external AI tools)\n   110→\n   111→**Patient Portal** (interfaces page, juvenile page):\n   112→- Integrates a portal allowing patients or family members to communicate electronically with healthcare providers\n   113→\n   114→**Hosting & Deployment**:\n   115→- Cloud-hosted (Kalleo Technologies, recommended), hybrid, or self-hosted options\n   116→\n   117→### Data & Content\n   118→\n   119→Based on the features and interfaces described above, Spark stores and manages the following data:\n   120→\n   121→**Clinical data**: Patient demographics, photos, facility locations, admission/discharge times (received from tracking/OMS/JMS systems). Medical records including encounter documentation, clinical notes, problem lists, medication lists, allergy/intolerance records, immunization records, vital signs, and clinical assessments. The (a)(1)-(a)(14) certification confirms CPOE data, drug interaction data, demographics, clinical decision support data, implantable device lists, and clinical quality measure data.\n   122→\n   123→**Behavioral health and dental records**: Explicitly mentioned as integrated into the unified patient chart alongside medical records.\n   124→\n   125→**Medication data**: eMAR records, e-prescribing history (including controlled substances via EPCS), medication orders/renewals/refills, drug substitution records, barcoding data, and 12-month SureScripts prescription history queries.\n   126→\n   127→**Orders and results**: Lab orders and results (bidirectional with lab vendors), radiology orders and interpretations (with optional images), medication orders.\n   128→\n   129→**Billing and financial data**: Claims data (Medicare, Medicaid, private), eligibility verification records, billing codes (auto-assigned from documentation), ERA/payment posting data, charges feed data, Medicaid 1115 waiver claims.\n   130→\n   131→**Sick call requests**: Inmate-initiated requests via phones/kiosks/tablets with confirmation and status tracking.\n   132→\n   133→**Tracking/custody data**: Patient demographic information, photos, locations within the facility, and admission/discharge events received from offender management/jail management systems (OMS/JMS).\n   134→\n   135→**Compliance and audit data**: Comprehensive audit trail of all system activity, compliance reporting data aligned with NCCHC/ACA/AJA standards.\n   136→\n   137→**Reporting data**: Hundreds of prebuilt report outputs across clinical, compliance, cost, and operational domains. CBI Dashboard analytics data (if add-on is used).\n   138→\n   139→**Interoperability records**: C-CDA documents, FHIR resources, health information exchange records (Carequality, HIE), US Marshals documentation, hospital records (lab results, transcriptions).\n   140→\n   141→**Portal data**: Patient/guardian communications and consent records (juvenile settings).\n   142→\n   143→**Notable**: The website does not mention appointment scheduling in detail beyond brief references to \"scheduling\" as a structured input. It's unclear how robust the scheduling module is. The system is not described as having a robust patient-facing portal in the correctional context (inmates typically don't have direct portal access), though guardian portal access is mentioned for juvenile settings.\n   144→\n   145→---\n   146→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016dP8u4xtrkAdMKh29av8Ho","type":"tool_result","content":"\t<!-- Basic Page Needs\r\n \t================================================== -->\r\n\t Open API Documentation | EMR Direct \r\n\t<!-- Mobile Specific Metas\r\n \t================================================== -->\r\n\t<!-- CSS\r\n \t================================================== -->\r\n\t<!-- Favicons\r\n\t================================================== -->\r\n\t<!-- Fonts\r\n\t================================================== -->\t\r\n\t<!-- Primary Page Layout\r\n\t================================================== -->\r\n Open API Documentation for Client Application Developers \r\n Interoperability Engine 2021 \r\n Updated Feb 5, 2026 \r\n 1. Introduction \r\nThis guide is written for third party developers, including patients, who are developing software applications for accessing Protected Health Information (PHI) based on this public API documentation which allows applications to query health data secured by a Data Holder. Data Holders wishing to publish such a public-facing API should have their Health IT vendor register as a developer integrator of EMR Direct Interoperability Engine services at https://www.emrdirect.com/subscribe-developer . \r\nALWAYS KEEP IN MIND THAT ONLINE DATA TRANSFER IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR PERSON-TO-PERSON COMMUNICATION OF URGENT OR CRITICAL MEDICAL INFORMATION. \r\nThis documentation contains general information and important security information. General information will be marked as:\r\n Note: \r\n and important security information will be marked as: \r\n Important: \r\n 2. General Concepts \r\n a. Application Access Requests \r\n The API is a read-only RESTful HL7 FHIR® R4 API and follows the syntax described at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/http.html . \r\nAll RESTful data access requests will be in the following format, in which the [base] URL will need to be obtained from the Data Holder, either directly or via directory information:\r\n GET [base]/[resource-specific parameters]… \r\n FHIR Bulk Data Access Group export is also supported as described in the Bulk Data Access IG. \r\n b.\tConnecting to the server \r\nThe server is accessed by clients through an https connection.\r\n Important: Local customer security policies must be in place to prevent unauthorized monitoring or eavesdropping of connections to the server. \r\n Important: Only TLS 1.2 connections are accepted. All plaintext connections will be refused. \r\n Note: Please limit your connection frequency to a value appropriate for your use case. Connection attempts which are more frequent than permitted by the bandwidth allocation for the data resource are not allowed. \r\n c. Authentication – Obtaining an Access Token \r\nPrior to making API requests, the client application must obtain an Access Token from the associated Authorization Server. The client software must support either the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant or client credentials grant flow as detailed in RFC 6749 . For authorization code flow, a client ID and client secret are required. If the client application does not have a client ID and client secret for this purpose, the client application may obtain a client ID and client secret using the dynamic client registration protocol by submitting the required client information to the registration endpoint as detailed in RFC 7591 , by accessing the registration endpoint URL with a browser and completing the online form, by completing the manual registration process at the EMR Direct website, or by using UDAP Dynamic Client Registration . Please see section 3(j) below for the list Client app attributes required for registration. For client credentials flow, a client ID and registered public key are required. Public keys for client credentials grant access may be registered using UDAP Dynamic Client Registration or by contacting the Data Holder directly.\r\nFor client applications using authorization code grants, end user authentication is performed using a username and authentication credentials provided by the Data Holder. A healthcare organization may reuse existing patient portal credentials for this purpose, in which case the authenticated username maps to a unique patient portal user on the resource holder’s side. The end user should obtain these credentials directly from the Data Holder healthcare organizations from which they wish to access data.\r\n Note: Usernames and authentication credentials are established and reset by the Data Holder.\r\n When an end user is directed to the authorization endpoint, the user will be presented with a login screen where they can enter their credentials for the healthcare organization they are accessing. If the correct credentials are supplied and the end user grants access to the client application, an authorization code will be returned to the client that the client application can use to obtain an access token through the token endpoint as described in RFC 6749. For client credentials flow, the application obtains an access token directly from the token endpoint without user interaction.\r\nEach healthcare organization has a unique base URL that is used to access its Authorization Server. The required endpoint URLs are of the following form: \r\n Endpoint URL \r\n Authorization \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/authz \r\n Token \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/token \r\n Registration \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/register \r\n Manage \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/manage \r\n Revoke \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/revoke \r\n The complete OAuth 2.0 endpoint URLs for a given FHIR endpoint are published in that Data Holder's well known SMART configuration endpoint, as per Section 8.2 of the HL7 SMART App Launch specification .\r\n Refresh tokens: Client apps that use the authorization code flow and can securely store refresh tokens may request a refresh token by including the offline_access scope in the initial authorization endpoint request. Note that the end user may remove this scope during the authorization process. If a refresh token is permitted, it will be returned together with the access token as per RFC 6749 , and can be exchanged for a new access token as per RFC 6749 . Refresh token lifetime defaults to 90 days (but may be longer or shorter depending on the Data Holder's institutional policies). Each refresh token may be used once; a replacement refresh token will be issued when the client app uses a valid refresh token to obtain a new access token. Note that refresh tokens are not issued to Client apps that support client credentials code flow as these clients can authenticate directly to the token endpoint to obtain a new access token.\r\n PKCE support: Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) as defined by RFC 7636 is supported for Client apps that use the authorization code flow. The use of PKCE by such clients is optional. If used, Client apps must use only the S256 code challenge method. Please refer to RFC 7636 for details on how to use PKCE in requests to the authorization and token endpoints.\r\nAll requests to the API must include the access token transmitted in the Authorization header of the HTTP request as a bearer token as illustrated in RFC 6750 . If the access token is missing, expired, or otherwise not valid for the requested operation, the API will return a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden response.\r\n 3. API Details \r\n a. Query a Specific Data Category Resource \r\n Client software must be capable of making HTTPS RESTful requests in accordance with the FHIR specification and consuming the FHIR Resources required by the United States Core Data for Interoperability ( USCDI ) or the FHIR Bulk Data Access specification. \r\n Resources returned conform to the resource profiles for HL7 FHIR R4 defined in the HL7 FHIR US Core Implementation Guide Release 3.1.1 found at https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1 . All of the US Core Resource Profiles are supported except the optional US Core Medication Profile, as this API uses inline medication codes to represent medications instead of References to separate Medication resources.\r\n General specifications for FHIR resources and the associated data elements can be found at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/resourcelist.html for other resource types without a US Core profile.\r\n Additional information for each required FHIR Resource or Data Element used to represent each data category can be found at the page above. For example, the Patient.name element is found at:\r\n https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/patient-definitions.html#Patient.name . The US Core FHIR IG profiles found at https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1/profiles.html provide additional information on the meanings of elements and codes used by these profiles.\r\n Choices of data types: The US Core resource profiles permit a number of data types for certain resource elements as indicated by the [x] notation in the corresponding element names. The following table lists the data types supported for elements where a choice of data types is allowed by the US Core FHIR IG. However, please note that a particular Data Holder may not return all supported data types for a given element.\r\n Resource Data Element Supported choices \r\n AllergyIntolerance.onset[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n CarePlan.scheduled[x] Timing, Period, string \r\n CarePlan.product[x] CodeableConcept, Reference \r\n Condition.onset[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n Condition.abatement[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n DiagnosticReport.effective[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Goal.start[x] date, CodeableConcept \r\n Goal.detail[x] Quantity, Range, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Ratio \r\n Goal.due[x] date \r\n Immunization.occurrence[x] dateTime, string \r\n Immunization.doseNumber[x] positiveInt, string \r\n Immunization.seriesDoses[x] positiveInt, string \r\n MedicationRequest.reported[x] boolean, Reference \r\n MedicationRequest.medication[x] CodeableConcept \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.asNeeded[x] boolean, CodeableConcept \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.doseAndRate.dose[x] Range, SimpleQuantity \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.doseAndRate.rate[x] Ratio, Range, SimpleQuantity \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.substitution.allowed[x] boolean, CodeableConcept \r\n Observation.effective[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Observation.value[x] Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampleData, time, dateTime, Period \r\n Observation.component.value[x] Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampleData, time, dateTime, Period \r\n Patient.deceased[x] boolean, dateTime \r\n Patient.multipleBirth[x] boolean, integer \r\n Procedure.performed[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Provenance.ocurred[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Choices of Reference resource types: The US Core resource profiles and the inherited FHIR R4 Observation Vital Signs profile permit a number of resource types to be referenced for certain \"Must Support\" resource elements where a value of type Reference is allowed for the corresponding element. The following table lists the resource types supported for such elements where a choice of referenced resource types is allowed. However, please note that a particular Data Holder may not return all supported resource types for a given element.\r\n Resource Data Element Supported choices \r\n CareTeam.participant.member US Core Patient, US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n DiagnosticReport.performer US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n DocumentReference.author US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization, US Core Patient \r\n MedicationRequest.reportedReference US Core Patient, US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n MedicationRequest.requester US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization, US Core Patient \r\n Observation.hasMember FHIR R4 Observation Vital Signs \r\n Provenance.agent.who US Core Practitioner, US Core Patient, US Core Organization \r\n b. Patient Selection \r\nTo search for patients, the application should request a bundle of Patient resources matching suitable search criteria. To facilitate this, client apps may include the following optional search parameters in a request for a Patient resource:\r\n Resource Data Element\t Search Parameter \r\n Patient.identifier\t identifier \r\n Patient.name\t name \r\n Patient.gender\t gender \r\n Patient.birthDate\t birthdate \r\n Please see the sections relating to search parameters in the US Core Patient Profile for details. Some Data Holders may support additional search parameters. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported search parameters or review the capability statement. \r\nFor example, to retrieve a bundle of Patient resources to which the app is authorized, where the patient's first or last name is Smith and the patient was born on July 4, 1976, the request could be formatted as: \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Patient?name=Smith&amp;birthdate=1976-07-04 \r\nThe API will return a bundle of all patients (possibly zero) matching the search criteria. Only patients for which the app has been authorized access will be included in the results. Each patient returned in the search results is assigned a unique patient ID that can be found in the Patient.id element of the corresponding Patient resource. This patient ID can be included in subsequent requests to retrieve additional resources for that specific patient. \r\n c. Query for a Specific Data Category \r\nThe Patient resource can be retrieved by specifying a specific patient ID or by performing a search as discussed in section 3(b). The remaining resource types listed in Section 3(a) can be accessed for a specific patient as a Bundle of resources by performing a search by resource type or by patient compartment and specifying the patient ID in the request. For example, to retrieve a bundle of Immunization resources containing all available immunization history for Patient 1234, the request could be formatted as: \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Immunization?patient=1234 \r\nThe following search terms can be used to isolate results for a single USCDI data class in cases where two or more data classes are represented by a single FHIR resource type:\r\n USCDI Data Class Search Parameter \r\n Health Concerns category=http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/CodeSystem/condition-category|health-concern \r\n Problems category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/condition-category|problem-list-item \r\n Smoking Status code=http://loinc.org|72166-2 \r\n Vital Signs category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|vital-signs \r\n Laboratory Tests &amp; Laboratory Values/Results category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|laboratory \r\nFor example, to retrieve the Smoking Status for Patient 1234, the request could be formatted as: \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Patient/1234/Observation?code=http://loinc.org|72166-2 \r\nEach search request will return a bundle of zero or more results meeting the search criteria.\r\n d. Query for All Data as a CCDA document \r\n CCDA documents can be accessed within DocumentReference resources using the $docref operation as described in the US Core FHIR IG at: https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1/OperationDefinition-docref.html . CCDAs are categorized as “Summary of Episode” Notes with LOINC code 34133-9. For example, to request a CCDA document covering all dates for patient 1234, the query could be formatted as: \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/DocumentReference/$docref?patient=1234 \r\nThe Base64 encoded CCDA XML data can be found in the DocumentReference.content.attachment.data element of the returned DocumentReference resource within the returned Bundle, if any.\r\n e. Query for a Subset of Data using Search Parameters \r\n The USCDI data classes or CCDA documents returned by the API may be filtered by supplying one or more optional search parameters, as detailed in the search parameter sections of the US Core Profiles for the corresponding resource type. The following table lists the supported search parameters for this purpose:\r\n Resource Data Element\t Search Parameter \r\n CarePlan.category\t category \r\n CareTeam.status\t status \r\n DiagnosticReport.code\t code \r\n DiagnosticReport.category\t category \r\n DiagnosticReport.effective\t date \r\n DocumentReference.type\t type \r\n DocumentReference.category\t category \r\n DocumentReference.date\t date \r\n Condition.category\t category \r\n MedicationStatement.status\t status \r\n MedicationRequest.intent\t intent \r\n Observation.code\t code \r\n Observation.category category \r\n Observation.effective\t date \r\n Patient.identifier\t identifier \r\n Patient.name\t name \r\n Patient.gender\t gender \r\n Patient.birthDate\t birthdate \r\n Condition.category\t category \r\n Procedure.performed\t date \r\nSome Data Holders may support additional search parameters. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported search parameters or review the capability statement.\r\n f. Error Handling \r\nIf the access token used in the request is invalid, expired, or the user has not been authorized to access the requested Resource, the API will return a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden HTTP response.\r\nIf the request cannot be processed for other reasons (temporarily unavailable, unsupported resource type, system error, etc.), the API will return a 400 Bad Request HTTP response containing an OperationOutcome Resource with additional information regarding the issue contained in the OperationOutcome.issue element.\r\nHandling of OAuth-related errors is detailed in RFC 6749 .\r\nHandling of dynamic client registration errors is detailed in RFC 7591 .\r\n g. Supported clinical scopes \r\nApps identify the types of clinical data they would like to access by specifying one or more clinical OAuth scopes in their registration and authorization requests. Clinical scopes follow the format defined in the SMART App Launch Framework 1.0.0. Please see https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/scopes-and-launch-context/index.html#scopes-for-requesting-clinical-data for additional details. Only read scopes are supported. Write scopes will be rejected. Applications may request patient-level, user-level, or system-level scopes for the following resource types:\r\n Resource \r\n AllergyIntolerance \r\n CarePlan \r\n CareTeam \r\n Condition \r\n Device \r\n DiagnosticReport \r\n DocumentReference \r\n Encounter \r\n Goal \r\n Group \r\n Immunization \r\n Location \r\n MedicationRequest \r\n Observation \r\n Organization \r\n Patient \r\n Practitioner \r\n PractitionerRole \r\n Procedure \r\n Provenance \r\n Some Data Holders may support additional resource types and clinical scopes. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported scopes or review the endpoint's capability statement to identify other resource types supported by that endpoint.\r\n Applications may also request \"wildcard\" scopes, e.g.: user/*.read \r\n h. OpenID Connect \r\nFor client apps that need to authenticate the end user using OpenID Connect, the server supports the required OpenID Connect functionality as specified in the SMART App Launch Framework version 1.0.0. Please refer to the following link for details: https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/scopes-and-launch-context/index.html#scopes-for-requesting-identity-data \r\n i. Other Security Considerations \r\n Revoking access to patient data: End users can sign in to the management endpoint listed above to terminate access that the user has previously granted to a client application. Client applications may request revocation of tokens by making a request to the Data Holder's revocation endpoint as described in RFC 7009 .\r\n j. Attributes required for registration \r\nTo register a client for authorization code flow, the following information is required:\r\n Developer Name \r\n the name of the entity that created the app \r\n Developer Representative \r\n the name of the person completing this registration \r\n Client App Name \r\n the human-readable name of the app \r\n Redirect URI \r\n the app's redirection URI (https only) \r\n Client App URI (optional) \r\n a web page about the client app (http or https) \r\n Logo URI (optional) \r\n a URI to retrieve an image file with the app's logo (https only) \r\n Terms of Service URI (optional) \r\n a web page to view the app's terms of service (http or https) \r\n Privacy Policy URI (optional) \r\n a web page to view the app's privacy policy (http or https) \r\n Contact email \r\n an email address where the app developer may be contacted (use mailto: scheme) \r\nAdditionally, the client app developer will select the applicable characteristics of their application from the following:","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"453dc40a-783e-4628-9d79-2bffe0022a82","uuid":"2901f6cd-e1ce-4e63-ae81-61454bca60b9","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\t<!-- Basic Page Needs\r\n \t================================================== -->\r\n\t Open API Documentation | EMR Direct \r\n\t<!-- Mobile Specific Metas\r\n \t================================================== -->\r\n\t<!-- CSS\r\n \t================================================== -->\r\n\t<!-- Favicons\r\n\t================================================== -->\r\n\t<!-- Fonts\r\n\t================================================== -->\t\r\n\t<!-- Primary Page Layout\r\n\t================================================== -->\r\n Open API Documentation for Client Application Developers \r\n Interoperability Engine 2021 \r\n Updated Feb 5, 2026 \r\n 1. Introduction \r\nThis guide is written for third party developers, including patients, who are developing software applications for accessing Protected Health Information (PHI) based on this public API documentation which allows applications to query health data secured by a Data Holder. Data Holders wishing to publish such a public-facing API should have their Health IT vendor register as a developer integrator of EMR Direct Interoperability Engine services at https://www.emrdirect.com/subscribe-developer . \r\nALWAYS KEEP IN MIND THAT ONLINE DATA TRANSFER IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR PERSON-TO-PERSON COMMUNICATION OF URGENT OR CRITICAL MEDICAL INFORMATION. \r\nThis documentation contains general information and important security information. General information will be marked as:\r\n Note: \r\n and important security information will be marked as: \r\n Important: \r\n 2. General Concepts \r\n a. Application Access Requests \r\n The API is a read-only RESTful HL7 FHIR® R4 API and follows the syntax described at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/http.html . \r\nAll RESTful data access requests will be in the following format, in which the [base] URL will need to be obtained from the Data Holder, either directly or via directory information:\r\n GET [base]/[resource-specific parameters]… \r\n FHIR Bulk Data Access Group export is also supported as described in the Bulk Data Access IG. \r\n b.\tConnecting to the server \r\nThe server is accessed by clients through an https connection.\r\n Important: Local customer security policies must be in place to prevent unauthorized monitoring or eavesdropping of connections to the server. \r\n Important: Only TLS 1.2 connections are accepted. All plaintext connections will be refused. \r\n Note: Please limit your connection frequency to a value appropriate for your use case. Connection attempts which are more frequent than permitted by the bandwidth allocation for the data resource are not allowed. \r\n c. Authentication – Obtaining an Access Token \r\nPrior to making API requests, the client application must obtain an Access Token from the associated Authorization Server. The client software must support either the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant or client credentials grant flow as detailed in RFC 6749 . For authorization code flow, a client ID and client secret are required. If the client application does not have a client ID and client secret for this purpose, the client application may obtain a client ID and client secret using the dynamic client registration protocol by submitting the required client information to the registration endpoint as detailed in RFC 7591 , by accessing the registration endpoint URL with a browser and completing the online form, by completing the manual registration process at the EMR Direct website, or by using UDAP Dynamic Client Registration . Please see section 3(j) below for the list Client app attributes required for registration. For client credentials flow, a client ID and registered public key are required. Public keys for client credentials grant access may be registered using UDAP Dynamic Client Registration or by contacting the Data Holder directly.\r\nFor client applications using authorization code grants, end user authentication is performed using a username and authentication credentials provided by the Data Holder. A healthcare organization may reuse existing patient portal credentials for this purpose, in which case the authenticated username maps to a unique patient portal user on the resource holder’s side. The end user should obtain these credentials directly from the Data Holder healthcare organizations from which they wish to access data.\r\n Note: Usernames and authentication credentials are established and reset by the Data Holder.\r\n When an end user is directed to the authorization endpoint, the user will be presented with a login screen where they can enter their credentials for the healthcare organization they are accessing. If the correct credentials are supplied and the end user grants access to the client application, an authorization code will be returned to the client that the client application can use to obtain an access token through the token endpoint as described in RFC 6749. For client credentials flow, the application obtains an access token directly from the token endpoint without user interaction.\r\nEach healthcare organization has a unique base URL that is used to access its Authorization Server. The required endpoint URLs are of the following form: \r\n Endpoint URL \r\n Authorization \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/authz \r\n Token \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/token \r\n Registration \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/register \r\n Manage \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/manage \r\n Revoke \t https://[baseOAuthURL]/revoke \r\n The complete OAuth 2.0 endpoint URLs for a given FHIR endpoint are published in that Data Holder's well known SMART configuration endpoint, as per Section 8.2 of the HL7 SMART App Launch specification .\r\n Refresh tokens: Client apps that use the authorization code flow and can securely store refresh tokens may request a refresh token by including the offline_access scope in the initial authorization endpoint request. Note that the end user may remove this scope during the authorization process. If a refresh token is permitted, it will be returned together with the access token as per RFC 6749 , and can be exchanged for a new access token as per RFC 6749 . Refresh token lifetime defaults to 90 days (but may be longer or shorter depending on the Data Holder's institutional policies). Each refresh token may be used once; a replacement refresh token will be issued when the client app uses a valid refresh token to obtain a new access token. Note that refresh tokens are not issued to Client apps that support client credentials code flow as these clients can authenticate directly to the token endpoint to obtain a new access token.\r\n PKCE support: Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) as defined by RFC 7636 is supported for Client apps that use the authorization code flow. The use of PKCE by such clients is optional. If used, Client apps must use only the S256 code challenge method. Please refer to RFC 7636 for details on how to use PKCE in requests to the authorization and token endpoints.\r\nAll requests to the API must include the access token transmitted in the Authorization header of the HTTP request as a bearer token as illustrated in RFC 6750 . If the access token is missing, expired, or otherwise not valid for the requested operation, the API will return a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden response.\r\n 3. API Details \r\n a. Query a Specific Data Category Resource \r\n Client software must be capable of making HTTPS RESTful requests in accordance with the FHIR specification and consuming the FHIR Resources required by the United States Core Data for Interoperability ( USCDI ) or the FHIR Bulk Data Access specification. \r\n Resources returned conform to the resource profiles for HL7 FHIR R4 defined in the HL7 FHIR US Core Implementation Guide Release 3.1.1 found at https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1 . All of the US Core Resource Profiles are supported except the optional US Core Medication Profile, as this API uses inline medication codes to represent medications instead of References to separate Medication resources.\r\n General specifications for FHIR resources and the associated data elements can be found at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/resourcelist.html for other resource types without a US Core profile.\r\n Additional information for each required FHIR Resource or Data Element used to represent each data category can be found at the page above. For example, the Patient.name element is found at:\r\n https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/patient-definitions.html#Patient.name . The US Core FHIR IG profiles found at https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1/profiles.html provide additional information on the meanings of elements and codes used by these profiles.\r\n Choices of data types: The US Core resource profiles permit a number of data types for certain resource elements as indicated by the [x] notation in the corresponding element names. The following table lists the data types supported for elements where a choice of data types is allowed by the US Core FHIR IG. However, please note that a particular Data Holder may not return all supported data types for a given element.\r\n Resource Data Element Supported choices \r\n AllergyIntolerance.onset[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n CarePlan.scheduled[x] Timing, Period, string \r\n CarePlan.product[x] CodeableConcept, Reference \r\n Condition.onset[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n Condition.abatement[x] dateTime, Age, Period, Range, string \r\n DiagnosticReport.effective[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Goal.start[x] date, CodeableConcept \r\n Goal.detail[x] Quantity, Range, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Ratio \r\n Goal.due[x] date \r\n Immunization.occurrence[x] dateTime, string \r\n Immunization.doseNumber[x] positiveInt, string \r\n Immunization.seriesDoses[x] positiveInt, string \r\n MedicationRequest.reported[x] boolean, Reference \r\n MedicationRequest.medication[x] CodeableConcept \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.asNeeded[x] boolean, CodeableConcept \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.doseAndRate.dose[x] Range, SimpleQuantity \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.doseAndRate.rate[x] Ratio, Range, SimpleQuantity \r\n MedicationRequest.doseageInstruction.substitution.allowed[x] boolean, CodeableConcept \r\n Observation.effective[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Observation.value[x] Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampleData, time, dateTime, Period \r\n Observation.component.value[x] Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampleData, time, dateTime, Period \r\n Patient.deceased[x] boolean, dateTime \r\n Patient.multipleBirth[x] boolean, integer \r\n Procedure.performed[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Provenance.ocurred[x] dateTime, Period \r\n Choices of Reference resource types: The US Core resource profiles and the inherited FHIR R4 Observation Vital Signs profile permit a number of resource types to be referenced for certain \"Must Support\" resource elements where a value of type Reference is allowed for the corresponding element. The following table lists the resource types supported for such elements where a choice of referenced resource types is allowed. However, please note that a particular Data Holder may not return all supported resource types for a given element.\r\n Resource Data Element Supported choices \r\n CareTeam.participant.member US Core Patient, US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n DiagnosticReport.performer US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n DocumentReference.author US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization, US Core Patient \r\n MedicationRequest.reportedReference US Core Patient, US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization \r\n MedicationRequest.requester US Core Practitioner, US Core Organization, US Core Patient \r\n Observation.hasMember FHIR R4 Observation Vital Signs \r\n Provenance.agent.who US Core Practitioner, US Core Patient, US Core Organization \r\n b. Patient Selection \r\nTo search for patients, the application should request a bundle of Patient resources matching suitable search criteria. To facilitate this, client apps may include the following optional search parameters in a request for a Patient resource:\r\n Resource Data Element\t Search Parameter \r\n Patient.identifier\t identifier \r\n Patient.name\t name \r\n Patient.gender\t gender \r\n Patient.birthDate\t birthdate \r\n Please see the sections relating to search parameters in the US Core Patient Profile for details. Some Data Holders may support additional search parameters. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported search parameters or review the capability statement. \r\nFor example, to retrieve a bundle of Patient resources to which the app is authorized, where the patient's first or last name is Smith and the patient was born on July 4, 1976, the request could be formatted as: \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Patient?name=Smith&amp;birthdate=1976-07-04 \r\nThe API will return a bundle of all patients (possibly zero) matching the search criteria. Only patients for which the app has been authorized access will be included in the results. Each patient returned in the search results is assigned a unique patient ID that can be found in the Patient.id element of the corresponding Patient resource. This patient ID can be included in subsequent requests to retrieve additional resources for that specific patient. \r\n c. Query for a Specific Data Category \r\nThe Patient resource can be retrieved by specifying a specific patient ID or by performing a search as discussed in section 3(b). The remaining resource types listed in Section 3(a) can be accessed for a specific patient as a Bundle of resources by performing a search by resource type or by patient compartment and specifying the patient ID in the request. For example, to retrieve a bundle of Immunization resources containing all available immunization history for Patient 1234, the request could be formatted as: \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Immunization?patient=1234 \r\nThe following search terms can be used to isolate results for a single USCDI data class in cases where two or more data classes are represented by a single FHIR resource type:\r\n USCDI Data Class Search Parameter \r\n Health Concerns category=http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/CodeSystem/condition-category|health-concern \r\n Problems category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/condition-category|problem-list-item \r\n Smoking Status code=http://loinc.org|72166-2 \r\n Vital Signs category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|vital-signs \r\n Laboratory Tests &amp; Laboratory Values/Results category=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|laboratory \r\nFor example, to retrieve the Smoking Status for Patient 1234, the request could be formatted as: \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/Patient/1234/Observation?code=http://loinc.org|72166-2 \r\nEach search request will return a bundle of zero or more results meeting the search criteria.\r\n d. Query for All Data as a CCDA document \r\n CCDA documents can be accessed within DocumentReference resources using the $docref operation as described in the US Core FHIR IG at: https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/STU3.1.1/OperationDefinition-docref.html . CCDAs are categorized as “Summary of Episode” Notes with LOINC code 34133-9. For example, to request a CCDA document covering all dates for patient 1234, the query could be formatted as: \r\nhttps://[baseURL]/DocumentReference/$docref?patient=1234 \r\nThe Base64 encoded CCDA XML data can be found in the DocumentReference.content.attachment.data element of the returned DocumentReference resource within the returned Bundle, if any.\r\n e. Query for a Subset of Data using Search Parameters \r\n The USCDI data classes or CCDA documents returned by the API may be filtered by supplying one or more optional search parameters, as detailed in the search parameter sections of the US Core Profiles for the corresponding resource type. The following table lists the supported search parameters for this purpose:\r\n Resource Data Element\t Search Parameter \r\n CarePlan.category\t category \r\n CareTeam.status\t status \r\n DiagnosticReport.code\t code \r\n DiagnosticReport.category\t category \r\n DiagnosticReport.effective\t date \r\n DocumentReference.type\t type \r\n DocumentReference.category\t category \r\n DocumentReference.date\t date \r\n Condition.category\t category \r\n MedicationStatement.status\t status \r\n MedicationRequest.intent\t intent \r\n Observation.code\t code \r\n Observation.category category \r\n Observation.effective\t date \r\n Patient.identifier\t identifier \r\n Patient.name\t name \r\n Patient.gender\t gender \r\n Patient.birthDate\t birthdate \r\n Condition.category\t category \r\n Procedure.performed\t date \r\nSome Data Holders may support additional search parameters. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported search parameters or review the capability statement.\r\n f. Error Handling \r\nIf the access token used in the request is invalid, expired, or the user has not been authorized to access the requested Resource, the API will return a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden HTTP response.\r\nIf the request cannot be processed for other reasons (temporarily unavailable, unsupported resource type, system error, etc.), the API will return a 400 Bad Request HTTP response containing an OperationOutcome Resource with additional information regarding the issue contained in the OperationOutcome.issue element.\r\nHandling of OAuth-related errors is detailed in RFC 6749 .\r\nHandling of dynamic client registration errors is detailed in RFC 7591 .\r\n g. Supported clinical scopes \r\nApps identify the types of clinical data they would like to access by specifying one or more clinical OAuth scopes in their registration and authorization requests. Clinical scopes follow the format defined in the SMART App Launch Framework 1.0.0. Please see https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/scopes-and-launch-context/index.html#scopes-for-requesting-clinical-data for additional details. Only read scopes are supported. Write scopes will be rejected. Applications may request patient-level, user-level, or system-level scopes for the following resource types:\r\n Resource \r\n AllergyIntolerance \r\n CarePlan \r\n CareTeam \r\n Condition \r\n Device \r\n DiagnosticReport \r\n DocumentReference \r\n Encounter \r\n Goal \r\n Group \r\n Immunization \r\n Location \r\n MedicationRequest \r\n Observation \r\n Organization \r\n Patient \r\n Practitioner \r\n PractitionerRole \r\n Procedure \r\n Provenance \r\n Some Data Holders may support additional resource types and clinical scopes. Contact the Data Holder for more information on the supported scopes or review the endpoint's capability statement to identify other resource types supported by that endpoint.\r\n Applications may also request \"wildcard\" scopes, e.g.: user/*.read \r\n h. OpenID Connect \r\nFor client apps that need to authenticate the end user using OpenID Connect, the server supports the required OpenID Connect functionality as specified in the SMART App Launch Framework version 1.0.0. Please refer to the following link for details: https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/scopes-and-launch-context/index.html#scopes-for-requesting-identity-data \r\n i. Other Security Considerations \r\n Revoking access to patient data: End users can sign in to the management endpoint listed above to terminate access that the user has previously granted to a client application. Client applications may request revocation of tokens by making a request to the Data Holder's revocation endpoint as described in RFC 7009 .\r\n j. Attributes required for registration \r\nTo register a client for authorization code flow, the following information is required:\r\n Developer Name \r\n the name of the entity that created the app \r\n Developer Representative \r\n the name of the person completing this registration \r\n Client App Name \r\n the human-readable name of the app \r\n Redirect URI \r\n the app's redirection URI (https only) \r\n Client App URI (optional) \r\n a web page about the client app (http or https) \r\n Logo URI (optional) \r\n a URI to retrieve an image file with the app's logo (https only) \r\n Terms of Service URI (optional) \r\n a web page to view the app's terms of service (http or https) \r\n Privacy Policy URI (optional) \r\n a web page to view the app's privacy policy (http or https) \r\n Contact email \r\n an email address where the app developer may be contacted (use mailto: scheme) \r\nAdditionally, the client app developer will select the applicable characteristics of their application from the following:","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01HDriH4fGhXggQCCPJeUyRg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CUXhGjnxo418fEqPvLJ9jv","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/correctek/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# CorrecTek — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.correctek.com/cost-disclosure-and-transparency/\n- CHPL ID: 10274\n- Product: Spark 7.1\n- Certification date: 2020-01-14\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n**1. Initial probe:**\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://www.correctek.com/cost-disclosure-and-transparency/\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36'\n```\nResult: HTTP 301 → `https://correctek.com/cost-disclosure-and-transparency/` → 301 → `https://correctek.com/cost-disclosure-and-transparency` → 200 OK. Content-Type: text/html. HubSpot-hosted site behind Cloudflare.\n\n**2. Page fetch with curl:**\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://correctek.com/cost-disclosure-and-transparency\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o /tmp/correctek-page.html\n```\nResult: 307KB HTML, but the page is client-side rendered (HubSpot JS SPA). No visible text extracted via standard HTML parsing — all content is injected via JavaScript.\n\n**3. Browser navigation:**\nNavigated to the URL in Chrome. The page rendered correctly. Title: \"Cost Disclosure & Transparency | CorrecTek\". The page is a standard ONC mandatory disclosures page listing certified criteria, cost information, and API details.\n\n**4. Searched for downloadable files:**\n```bash\ngrep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|csv|json|doc|docx|yaml|yml)[^\"]*\"' /tmp/correctek-page.html\n```\nResult: Only one file link found: `https://appstudio.interopengine.com/partner/fhirR4endpoints-umc.json` (FHIR endpoints JSON for their g(10) API).\n\n**5. Located the b(10) EHI Export section:**\nFound at the bottom of the certification criteria table. The entire b(10) documentation is:\n\n> §170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export*\n>\n> *EHI can be exported in PDF or C-CDA format. Records for a patient are exported to one or more PDF/C-CDA files. The files created by the export are saved to a folder specified by the us\n\nThe text is truncated on the live page — it cuts off at \"the us\". Confirmed via Wayback Machine (2024-04-18 capture) that the complete sentence reads \"...saved to a folder specified by the **user**.\" — a minor content authoring error likely introduced during a site update.\n\n**6. Downloaded the FHIR endpoints JSON:**\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://appstudio.interopengine.com/partner/fhirR4endpoints-umc.json\" -o fhirR4endpoints-umc.json\n```\nResult: An empty FHIR Bundle with no entries: `{\"resourceType\":\"Bundle\",\"type\":\"collection\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-02-07T14:37:24-08:00\"}`. No customer endpoints are listed.\n\n**7. Checked for additional EHI documentation:**\n- Sitemap (`/sitemap.xml`): Only one disclosure-related URL exists: the cost-disclosure-and-transparency page itself.\n- Probed common paths: `/ehi`, `/ehi-export`, `/interoperability`, `/onc`, `/compliance`, `/legal`, `/api`, `/fhir`, `/documentation` — all returned 404.\n- The linked Interoperability Engine Open API Documentation (https://www.interopengine.com/2021/open-api-documentation.html) is a detailed (g)(10) FHIR R4/US Core API guide from EMR Direct. It documents the SMART on FHIR authorization flow, USCDI data classes, and Bulk Data Access. This is entirely the g(10) standardized API — not the b(10) EHI export.\n\n**8. Checked Wayback Machine:**\n```bash\ncurl -s \"http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=www.correctek.com/cost-disclosure-and-transparency&output=text&fl=timestamp,statuscode&from=20230101&limit=20\"\n```\n10 captures from 2020–2025, all returning 200. The 2024-04-18 capture confirmed the complete (untruncated) EHI text. No additional EHI documentation was ever present on any captured version.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation from CorrecTek consists of a **single sentence** on their mandatory disclosures page:\n\n> *EHI can be exported in PDF or C-CDA format. Records for a patient are exported to one or more PDF/C-CDA files. The files created by the export are saved to a folder specified by the user.*\n\nThat is the complete technical documentation for their 170.315(b)(10) EHI Export certification. There is:\n\n- **No data dictionary** — no listing of what data fields, tables, or categories are exported\n- **No export format specification** — no details on the PDF structure or C-CDA template/profile used\n- **No schema files** — no XSD, JSON Schema, or other machine-readable format definition\n- **No sample data** — no example export files\n- **No user guide** — no instructions for initiating the export, no screenshots of the export interface\n- **No API documentation** specific to the export (the linked API docs are for the g(10) FHIR API)\n\nThe only additional artifact is a FHIR R4 endpoints JSON file linked on the page, which is an empty Bundle with no entries — suggesting either no customers are currently integrated with the FHIR API, or the file is a placeholder.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThis is where the single-sentence documentation creates the biggest gap. CorrecTek Spark is a **correctional healthcare EHR** that stores a wide range of patient data:\n\n**Known data domains (from product research):**\n- Demographics, contacts, insurance/enrollment\n- Medical encounters and clinical notes\n- Behavioral health records\n- Dental records\n- Medication management (eMAR, EPCS, e-prescribing)\n- Lab orders and results\n- Radiology/imaging orders and results\n- Allergies, immunizations, vital signs, problem lists\n- Billing (claims, eligibility, ERA posting, Medicaid 1115 waiver)\n- Sick call requests\n- Inmate tracking/custody data (received from jail management systems)\n- Care plans, referrals\n- Custom correctional healthcare forms (intake screenings, NCCHC/ACA compliance forms)\n\n**What the documentation tells us about coverage:** Almost nothing. The export is described as \"PDF or C-CDA format\" — but there is no specification of which data domains are included. The key questions are completely unanswered:\n\n- **Billing data**: Not mentioned. PDF/C-CDA formats are clinical document standards that don't naturally represent billing records (claims, ERA postings, eligibility data).\n- **Behavioral health records**: Not mentioned. These are critical in a correctional EHR. Are they included in the C-CDA?\n- **Dental records**: Not mentioned. Spark explicitly integrates dental into the unified chart — is dental data exported?\n- **Correctional-specific data**: Intake screenings, sick call requests, custody/tracking data, compliance documentation — none of these have natural C-CDA representations.\n- **Medication administration records (eMAR)**: The eMAR is a core correctional nursing workflow. Is it captured in the C-CDA, or only active medication lists?\n- **Lab and imaging results**: Likely partially covered by C-CDA, but no confirmation.\n\nThe statement \"Records for a patient are exported to one or more PDF/C-CDA files\" could mean anything from a single-page clinical summary to a comprehensive dump of every document in the chart. Without a data dictionary or content specification, it's impossible to assess coverage.\n\n**Likely reality:** Given that the export uses PDF and C-CDA:\n- C-CDA will cover the standard clinical summary data (demographics, problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, vital signs, lab results, procedures) — essentially the USCDI/US Core subset.\n- PDF may capture additional clinical notes and documents.\n- Billing, dental, behavioral health-specific assessments, correctional forms, eMAR details, and custody data are almost certainly **not** included in a standard C-CDA export unless CorrecTek has done significant custom work (which they haven't documented).\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: PDF and/or C-CDA (the asterisk with \"PDF or C-CDA\" suggests the user may have a choice, or different data may go to different formats).\n- **C-CDA**: No version, template, or profile specified. No indication of which C-CDA document type (CCD, Discharge Summary, etc.). No section-level detail.\n- **PDF**: No detail on structure — could be a simple printout of the chart, or structured clinical documents rendered as PDF.\n- **Delivery**: Files saved to a local folder. No mention of encryption, compression, or integrity verification.\n\nThe choice of PDF/C-CDA is concerning for a b(10) export. C-CDA is designed for clinical summaries — it covers the standard clinical data classes well but has no natural representation for:\n- Detailed billing records\n- Correctional-specific workflows (intake screenings, sick call management)\n- eMAR administration details\n- Dental charts\n- Custom form data\n\nA vendor that has genuinely addressed b(10) for a correctional EHR would need to export data that goes well beyond what C-CDA can represent. The absence of any additional export format (database dump, CSV, custom XML) for non-clinical data suggests this export likely covers only the clinical summary portion of the record.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Extremely poor.** One truncated sentence is not documentation. A developer receiving this export would have no way to:\n- Know what data to expect\n- Parse the C-CDA reliably (no profile/template guidance)\n- Verify completeness (no data dictionary to compare against)\n- Automate import (no schema or sample files)\n\nThis is the absolute minimum a vendor could provide — a single sentence saying \"we export in these formats\" — without any substantive technical detail. It reads as a compliance checkbox rather than genuine documentation.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Field-level documentation**: None\n- **Data types/value sets**: None\n- **Entity relationships**: None\n- **Sample data**: None\n- **Versioning/change history**: None\n- **Export instructions**: None (just \"saved to a folder specified by the user\")\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://correctek.com/cost-disclosure-and-transparency\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: yes (HubSpot JS-rendered page; curl returns empty HTML)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (b(10) section is on the single disclosure page)\n- Anti-bot issues: Cloudflare present but not blocking; main issue is JS rendering requirement\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- **Truncated text**: The b(10) description is cut off at \"the us\" on the live page (missing \"er.\" to complete \"the user.\"). Confirmed complete text via Wayback Machine.\n- **JS-rendered page**: curl cannot extract visible content; browser required for text extraction.\n- **Empty FHIR endpoints JSON**: The linked endpoints file contains an empty FHIR Bundle with no entries.\n- **No additional documentation found**: Sitemap, path probing, and Google searches returned no additional EHI-specific pages or documents.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":240,"cache_read_input_tokens":76395,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":240},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"453dc40a-783e-4628-9d79-2bffe0022a82","uuid":"71e6b8e8-5352-495e-a867-386e3cd76083"}

Without a data dictionary or content specification, it's impossible to assess coverage.\n\n**Likely reality:** Given that the export uses PDF and C-CDA:\n- C-CDA will cover the standard clinical summary data (demographics, problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, vital signs, lab results, procedures) — essentially the USCDI/US Core subset.\n- PDF may capture additional clinical notes and documents.\n- Billing, dental, behavioral health-specific assessments, correctional forms, eMAR details, and custody data are almost certainly **not** included in a standard C-CDA export unless CorrecTek has done significant custom work (which they haven't documented).\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: PDF and/or C-CDA (the asterisk with \"PDF or C-CDA\" suggests the user may have a choice, or different data may go to different formats).\n- **C-CDA**: No version, template, or profile specified. No indication of which C-CDA document type (CCD, Discharge Summary, etc.). No section-level detail.\n- **PDF**: No detail on structure — could be a simple printout of the chart, or structured clinical documents rendered as PDF.\n- **Delivery**: Files saved to a local folder. No mention of encryption, compression, or integrity verification.\n\nThe choice of PDF/C-CDA is concerning for a b(10) export. C-CDA is designed for clinical summaries — it covers the standard clinical data classes well but has no natural representation for:\n- Detailed billing records\n- Correctional-specific workflows (intake screenings, sick call management)\n- eMAR administration details\n- Dental charts\n- Custom form data\n\nA vendor that has genuinely addressed b(10) for a correctional EHR would need to export data that goes well beyond what C-CDA can represent. The absence of any additional export format (database dump, CSV, custom XML) for non-clinical data suggests this export likely covers only the clinical summary portion of the record.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Extremely poor.** One truncated sentence is not documentation. A developer receiving this export would have no way to:\n- Know what data to expect\n- Parse the C-CDA reliably (no profile/template guidance)\n- Verify completeness (no data dictionary to compare against)\n- Automate import (no schema or sample files)\n\nThis is the absolute minimum a vendor could provide — a single sentence saying \"we export in these formats\" — without any substantive technical detail.
